issuing_body: U.S. Attorney's Office, District of Minnesota
title: In Landmark Sentence, Feeding Our Future Scheme Leader Sentenced to 28 Years in Prison
notes: Retrieved via the in-browser fetch tool after both a plain WebFetch and a curl-with-browser-UA attempt returned only an Akamai bot-verification interstitial (bm-verify challenge page), not article content. Cited on the live /status/ page (status/index.html) without this corpus previously having captured it; this record closes that provenance gap.
supports: United States District Judge Nancy E. Brasel sentenced Abdiaziz Shafii Farah, age 36, on August 6, 2025 to 28 years in prison followed by 3 years of supervised release for his role in the Feeding Our Future fraud scheme.
Farah was ordered to pay restitution in the amount of $47,920,514.

In June 2024, following a seven-week trial before Judge Brasel, a federal jury convicted Farah of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, conspiracy to commit federal programs bribery, false statements on a passport application, conspiracy to commit money laundering, two counts of federal programs bribery, six counts of wire fraud, and 11 counts of money laundering.
Farah personally pocketed more than $8 million during 18 months of involvement in the scheme, according to the release.

Farah pleaded guilty in a separate juror-bribery case and was, as of this release, pending sentencing in that case before Judge David S. Doty; today's 28-year sentence does not reflect the juror-bribery conduct.
The release describes the underlying scheme as exploiting a federally funded child nutrition program during the COVID-19 pandemic and characterizes it as a $300 million fraud scheme.
does_not_support: This release predates and does not itself state Farah's later juror-bribery sentence (120 months, imposed 2026-07-22); that is reported in a separate USAO-MN release already in this corpus.
This release does not isolate a single case-level 'alleged loss' figure distinct from the $47,920,514 restitution order; do not conflate restitution with a charging-document alleged-loss figure.
